minutes.headline: Select Board voted 3-2 to pay the two school bus companies the school committee's approved amounts for closed-school months.
minutes.summary: The board heard from the two school transportation companies, the school business manager and the superintendent about payment requests for the spring school closure, debated precedent and tax money, and approved the school committee's amounts by roll call. It also made two interim appointments, authorized posting two Parks Commission vacancies under the new charter, set a November special town meeting schedule, and declined to recommend naming a brook. The finance director's quarterly report was postponed because of audio problems.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 3-2 to pay the two school bus companies the amounts the school committee approved for the spring school closure.
A motion not to support any payment to the bus companies failed for lack of a second before the 3-2 roll call vote.
The board authorized the town manager to post two new Parks Commission vacancies for joint appointment until the next annual election.
The board accepted the special town meeting timeline, with the warrant opening Wednesday September 2, and tabled the FY2021 budget discussion to next week.
The board voted 5-0 not to recommend naming a tributary after a non-resident, and will send that response to the federal naming board.

why_it_matters: The bus payments for months when schools were closed come from the town budget, mostly taxes, and the 3-2 split shows the board divided over paying private contractors for service not delivered.
The special town meeting, where residents will vote on articles, and the FY2021 budget discussion are both still unsettled, as are the safety arrangements for attending in person.
watch_next: Next week: the finance director's fourth quarter report, the FY2021 budget discussion and the special town meeting articles, plus a revised meeting safety plan.
Parks Commission interviews later in the month for the two interim seats.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary:
The two records agree on the main votes: both appointments, the 3-2 bus payment of $94,000 and $41,112, and the special town meeting schedule. They also match on most figures and on the tabling decisions.

Our minutes record two 5-0 votes that the official minutes do not show: the Parks Commission posting and the Baelish Brook recommendation. They also read the third warrant as $31,887.93 against the official $631,887.93, and they name the chair as McCarthy where the official minutes give Alonzo.
